A user says their Google account mysteriously stopped working about 6 years earlier and they lost all their email, contacts, and calendars. Emails and support forms got no response from Google. They no longer trust Google with data they care about and wish the export tool worked for deactivated accounts.

When Google Takeout export launched, one user found only the Calendar backup option available; the Gmail option was not yet shown. Calendar data could be downloaded right away, while Gmail export was rolled out gradually.

Samsung smart fridge owners could not sign in to Google Calendar. The problem was reported in Nov 2014, resolved for some models in Feb 2015, and still not fixed for all fridges in Dec 2015. Samsung support only advised restarting the fridge and checking the timezone. One owner bought the fridge so his wife could keep up with his calendar.

During an outage, users in France, UK, Germany, Poland, Spain, Brazil, India, Canada, the US and elsewhere reported Google Calendar web returning 404s, with intermittent 500/503s. One user noted the mobile app was still working.
Before the full outage, one user saw blank calendar pages from the end of 2019 onward, while June and July 2019 still showed. Another said months after July disappeared, then the site went fully 404.
A user complained that Google's Apps status dashboard showed nothing during the Calendar outage: 'What's the point of a status site that doesn't reflect the status?'
One user said the outage was especially chaotic for business GSuite users and wished for an offline/local cache option for cloud-hosted calendars.

A user moved off Google Calendar years ago to self-hosted Radicale, used with Thunderbird and DavDroid/DavX for events and contacts. They acknowledged GCal is rarely down but objected to Google harvesting data for advertising.

Welcoming the redesigned mobile app, one user said the previous Calendar app felt 'stuck in 2009' and the new one seems actually designed for small screens. Another said the Material Design experience made them a Google fanboy again. A third complained the web version had not been updated.

A user complained that the web version doesn't support the browser back button. Hitting back from an event screen often exits the calendar site entirely instead of returning to the calendar view, forcing use of the in-app JS back button.
A user said Google Calendar still lacks a month view with legible event labels, while the default Samsung calendar app 'pulls it off beautifully'.

A user criticized the new agenda/stream view for not showing empty stretches of time. Seeing at a glance that nothing is coming up in the next two hours matters to them, and classic calendar views show that.
A user reported already getting spam through calendar invites that are auto-added before they can see them. They want a private calendar without invites or auto-added events from email.
A user was shocked that Android's default Google Calendar app doesn't support CalDAV or any calendar server besides Google's, unless you add a separate CalDAV sync app.

A longtime user missed the early Google Calendar feature of typing natural text like 'Dinner tomorrow at 7:30pm at Foobar restaurant' to create an event automatically, and was glad it seemed to be returning.
A user complained you still can't post simple HTML or RTF into event descriptions in the web version of Google Calendar.

A user said their German employer banned all Google products except search for work, including Calendar, over privacy concerns. They wished email-to-event conversion ran locally rather than by scanning emails on Google's servers.
An iOS user called the existing calendar app options terrible and looked forward to an official Google Calendar app for iOS, since they already store contacts and calendar on Google.
'All I want in Google calendar is a log of changes to the calendar itself.' The user wants change history for calendar edits.
